To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the p16INK4aNuclear Score is a promising biomarker to identify high‐grade lesions in cervical smears and that this biomarker is suitable to be used in liquid‐based samples.

the p16INK4 score is a reliable biomarker for the detection of cervical squamous cell abnormalities and that it is superior to the Bethesda classification in predicting the severity of squamous cell abnormalities.
the p16INK4A nuclear scoring system can be successfully used to identify abnormal cells on liquid‐based cytologic specimens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of a nuclear score (NS) for p16INKA4a‐staining cervical squamous cells and its application for the identification of abnormal cervical cells in liquid‐ based cytology samples.
the evaluation of a nuclear score to identify p16INK4A‐stained cells in liquid‐ based cytology samples.

the development and application of new methods in the fields of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, molecular biology, and biophysics, and the application of these methods in the field of medicine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p16INK4A immunocytochemistry is a useful adjunct to cytologic evaluation of liquid‐based cytologic samples, especially when the cytologic diagnosis is indeterminate or inconclusive.

p16INK4A is an excellent biomarker for high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) and invasive cervical cancer, and is a good biomarker for atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASCUS) and low‐grade squamous epithelial lesions (LSIL).

a p16INK4aNuclear Score of ≥ 1 is a reliable and reproducible marker of high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) in liquid‐based samples, but that a score of 0 is not a reliable indicator of absence of HSIL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p16INK4A is a useful marker for the identification of abnormal cells in cervical samples, but the sensitivity and specificity of this marker is not as high as we would like.

the nuclear score for p 16 INK4a‐staining is a reliable marker for identifying high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions in liquid‐based cervical cytology samples and may be a useful adjunct to the Papanicolaou test.
the p16INK4A nuclear score is an effective and reliable biomarker for identifying cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and cervical cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a p16INK4A score can be used to identify cervical squamous cells with high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and squamous cell carcinoma in liquid‐based samples.
p16INK4A immunocytochemistry can be used in liquid‐based samples to detect abnormal cells, including those that are HPV positive but not cytologically detectable.
p16INK4A is a very good biomarker to detect cervical dysplasia, and it can be used as an additional biomarker in cervical cancer screening.
